- **Cache-side current-shape reads now say why no shape was selected (#3934).** On a thread whose only `## Current shape (as of pass-N)` comments were dropped by the #2307 maintainer-authorship filter, the sidecar builder, cache `content.md`, and `issue:ingest` returned a bare null -- indistinguishable from a thread that never had a shape -- so a cache-reading agent fell back to the stale issue body. All three now report the reason, naming discarded comments by id and author association only, never comment text. Advisory: `--strict`, the maintainer-authored count, and every thread with a selected maintainer shape are byte-identical to before, and `MAINTAINER_ASSOCIATIONS` still refuses forgeries. Refs #1152, #1870, #2307, #3156.
- **On Grok, the worktree lease no longer denies the session holding it (#3873).** The host publishes `GROK_SESSION_ID`; Directive read only `DEFT_SESSION_ID`, so the hook presented an empty actor, the write gate read that as a stranger to the live lease, and the denial named the holder's own session id back at it. Every tool-call edit had to be routed through the shell for the length of a run. Grok now resolves its owner from the host variable in the hook process, `deft session:start` is bound to the same canonical owner so the lease it claims is the one later writes present, and the denial a refused caller sees names the identity it actually presented -- so `occupancy:grant --child-session-id=<id>` is runnable instead of naming an id nothing can grant. Nothing became more permissive: a caller with no identity is still denied, a malformed host variable fails closed, and an ambient `DEFT_SESSION_ID` that contradicts the host owner fails closed. Refs #3611, #3755, #3156.

- A brief stranded in `xbrief/active/` by one merge no longer reddens the merge gate on every other open PR. `verify:orphan-active` now runs candidate-scoped inside `check:merge` (`--changed-only`), evaluating only the briefs the branch's own diff touches, so unrelated PRs stop failing on residue they did not create and two single-brief lifecycle PRs no longer block each other. The repo-wide sweep still runs at the delivery tip, on the bare verb, and on the after-merge `--issue N` gate, and the linked-PR/open-issue signature is unchanged. `verify:consumer-check-contract` gained the matching composition rule: fail-closed for this repo's own aggregates, a named warning for deposits still on the unscoped form (#3893).

- **A design-critique synthesis can no longer clear ingest by citing a verified-claims table that is not one (#3932).** Table resolution scanned every citation for the first table-shaped body and never checked that citation's kind, so a record naming a table id that is not a table still cleared whenever some other cited comment happened to be table-shaped -- an arc comment that quotes the table heading was enough. A typed `verified-claims table <id>` citation now decides resolution and a generic citation can neither satisfy nor mask it, and every table-kind citation in one record must name the same table, so one valid claim cannot launder a ghost beside it (new `ambiguous-table-cite` block reason). Records that cite their table only by permalink or bare `comment` id keep resolving as they do today -- those forms are untyped by design, and narrowing the citation grammar is not part of this fix. Closes #3932. Refs #3831, #3929, #3806.

### Removed

### Security

- **Residual: Grok Build shell-write gating is a cooperative guardrail, not a closed bypass (#3987 / #3997).** Matcher coverage for `run_terminal_command` shipped with #3983. Recogniser recall is about 47%; destinations that are shell variables, compounds, or junctions still skip the gate. Lease-refresh liveness for writes the classifier never sees stays on #3987. The fail-open posture is bound on #3997. Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex are unaffected.
## [0.108.0] - 2026-08-29

> Worktree leases admit named child sessions, a missing hook runtime is now recoverable instead of an opaque lockout, and lifecycle gates stop trusting stale issue state.

- Fixed: local Cursor sessions no longer misread as cloud, so SCM-dependent gates stop silently skipping when a healthy gh login is available. Cursor-managed VMs are now denied host credentials by a positive agent/runtime=managed metadata read that still lands if an earlier probe failed, an ambiguous Cursor runtime requires an explicit DEFT_GITHUB_AUTH_MODE=host-gh opt-in, and skipped gates now report why (#3859).

### Added
- Added — article-review Step 6.5 process-only critic pass before filing, with Step 5 mechanism inventory and Critic verdict section on filed issues. Refs #5694.
- Added — Prefer-A Recut-2 for `feedback:file`: complete open inventory dedup, closed retained-count window (500) with disposition tokens, open-match evidence comment (`commented-open-duplicate`), and `--on-closed=comment|create-anyway` without reopen. Refs #5099.
- Added — Helpers for reviewing a brief without creating a GitHub issue. These support file-based critic results, retained review records, and returning the accepted remedy to the same brief. Refs #5486.
### Changed
- **Bind record filenames no longer carry a session-id prefix (#3768).** Records under `.deft/session-binds/` are named by their 24-hex SHA-256 slice alone, so a directory listing exposes no fragment of a session id. Lookup stays derivable from the id in O(1) — no index, no directory scan. Records written under the old prefixed name are read-accepted until the next bind supersedes them, so freshness pins are not orphaned. Closes #3768. Refs #3117, #3754.

### Fixed
- **A release cut no longer dies on an empty-stderr exit 1 once a repo has more than 1 MB of open issues (#3903).** The SCM `call()` helper ran its subprocess without a stdout ceiling, so it inherited Node's 1 MB default: the paginated open-issue inventory release Step 3 depends on (4.1 MB on this repo) aborted with ENOBUFS, and the truncated capture surfaced as exit 1 with no reason and a misleading gh-auth hint. `call()` now passes the shared 64 MB ceiling and reports `error.message` when a spawn-level failure leaves stderr empty, so an overflow or a timeout kill always names itself. The same ceiling now covers four more capture sites whose payload is unbounded: cached `task` verb output, the system-of-record base-ref diff, projection provider commands, and `git show` of a tracked blob. The empty-reason fallback is one shared helper, so those sites report an overflow instead of an empty failure too. Refs #1867, #3752.
- **A third-party comment can no longer make `verify:ac` read a file and report what is in it (#3835).** Clause derivation no longer takes an artifact path out of issue or comment prose; the walk reads only paths the brief declares on `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope`, and an undeclared path is refused before any filesystem access with a refusal that reads the same whichever string the prose asked about. Two gate seams close with it: a clause must verify against its own bound artifact rather than being covered by a sibling, and a walk that verified nothing no longer relabels an empty acceptance run as verified. Refs #3323, #3826, #3840, #3842, #3819.
- **A session the write gate is about to deny can no longer rewrite the occupant's ritual state (#3769).** The mutation hook ran the gated ritual verifier before the occupancy verdict, and that verifier executes `agent_hooks` and rebinds a forward HEAD — both of which write `.deft/ritual-state.json`. Occupancy now decides first, and a denied session reads the ritual through a no-write inspect, so the owner's record is byte-identical after the refusal and is never retitled. Compact keeps its always-allow path outside the mutation gates, and its stale-mark stays fail-open: it writes even when no acting identity can be bound, on the recorded trade that an unidentified compact re-arms the owner rather than leaving a silently valid bind. A lease that transfers while verification is already running is covered too: the in-flight write is refused instead of landing on the new owner record. Closes #3769. Refs #3613, #3433, #3611, #2113, #3738.
- **The stale-origin refusal now names a recovery that works from the state it prints in (#3828).** `xbrief:preflight` told an agent to bump `xBRIEFInfo.updated` and then closed with `scope:activate`, a verb that hard-errors on a brief already in `active/`. It now names the interim stamp path -- `scope:block` then `scope:unblock`, which run in place, require and restore `running`, and write the field the check reads. That pair is interim: it records a `blocked` -> `running` transition for a brief that was never blocked, and #3857 owns the verb that records the acknowledgement honestly. When the origin cannot be fetched or compared, the refusal says so instead of offering a stamp that would not clear it. The scope-not-ready write refusal also stops claiming Shell coverage it does not have: `plan.policy.runtimeAuthority.shellDestForms` defaults to `off`, under which no Shell command is behind that deny, where the old sentence advertised `rm` / `git restore` coverage and named `python -c` as the only gap. The originally filed defect -- a stale-origin deny on the host write path -- was released-binary lag: #3736 removed origin freshness from that path and the observed denials came from a released CLI that predates it. Closes #3828. Refs #309, #3363, #3736, #3794, #3857.
- **A write in a linked worktree is now judged by that worktree's active scope, not the primary checkout's (#3794).** Commit 1 moved occupancy and ritual onto the tree a direct write lands in; active scope, the story `file_scope` fence and the assist-scratch classification still followed the hook payload root, so a swarm worker's write was measured against the wrong tree. All three now resolve against the admitted `effectiveRoot`, which is accepted only when its `--git-common-dir` matches the payload root's. Authz grant scoping, the authz audit trail, the `.deft-directive-disable` kill-switch and the #2885 outside-root carve-out stay pinned to the payload root. The scope and `file_scope` refusals now name both trees and say which one the recovery has to run in, because once the two roots differ no single "project root" satisfies the instruction. **Migration:** `.deft-scratch/` is an assist-scratch prefix, so every file in a worktree under `.deft-scratch/worktrees/` used to classify as disposable scratch and skip ritual, occupancy and scope under assist or ephemeral posture. Those writes are gated normally now; an assist-posture worktree agent that relied on the bypass must run `deft scope:activate` in its own worktree. Genuine scratch inside the worktree (`<worktree>/.deft-scratch/`) still classifies as scratch. Refs #3807, #3613, #3433, #2885.
- **The design-critique contract now guards sibling completeness the same way in all seven places (#3850).** Five bind guards required siblings “named on the panel-deposit” while two already read “same-round siblings remain unposted”, so a parent reading one locus got a different rule than a parent reading another. All seven now carry the deposit-independent wording that already existed. The contract also states plainly that panel completeness is a real obligation on the parent that no code observes, so no reader infers a gate that is not there. Prose only: no gate reads deposit contents, and no new predicate is introduced. Closes #3850. Refs #3824, #3848, #3851.
- **The design-critique router now orients readers on sibling isolation and adjudication (#3848).** The thin skill states that same-round critics cannot read each other's posts through the thread, names parent and operator steps in a motion-shape reference without duplicating comment-lead chips, and scopes the EXIT line to operator dispatch. Pack source edit plus `references/motion-shape.md`. Successor-lean subject ambiguity (#3851) is out of scope. Closes #3848.
- **A design-critique synthesis written in the house style now clears ingest, and mixed formatting no longer waives the verified-claims-table requirement (#3831).** `content/contracts/design-critique.md` publishes the citation grammar as a closed set — bare decimal, colon form, balanced single-backtick decimal, emphasised keyword, and the two canonical comment permalinks — and one parser now answers both questions the ingest predicate asks, so a decorated table id blocks as `missing-table-cite` instead of returning `complete` with a null table id. A position predicate refuses fenced, inline-code, blockquoted, struck-through, and negated occurrences that used to clear as affirmative citations, so the accept set is narrower on net. Clearance is set membership against the latest successor lean, so citing the superseded lean first — which the contract requires — no longer blocks with a message asserting a recut that never happened, and block details now report what was scanned and what was found. Refs #3806, #3796, #3156.
- **An issue's own acceptance list is now what gates it, instead of prose scraped out of its comment thread (#3826).** Clause derivation only read `item.narrative.Acceptance`, but ingested criteria live in `item.title` with an empty `narrative`, so a declared acceptance surface was invisible and derivation transcribed path-bearing bullets out of the issue discussion instead. On #3794 that produced 58 clauses from 84,535 characters of thread while 13 human-written criteria sat unread in the same brief; 55 of the 58 bound paths did not exist, which blocked the brief and left it on one machine. Derivation now reads `item.title` when the narrative is empty and treats a declared `plan.items` surface as the clause set, so an acceptance-shaped heading buried in the comment thread cannot become the gate. Re-deriving #3794 yields its 13 declared criteria and zero failed clauses; #3819 yields its 10. Separately, an absent artifact no longer counts as verified because the words "does not exist" appear somewhere in the clause text — that match was against the whole clause, so on #3794 a bare `git.ts` in analysis prose was the only passing clause and the sole thing satisfying the walk's `verified > 0` requirement. Absence is now unverifiable; a clause the shipped artifact contradicts still fails. No clause-count cap is introduced, and briefs that already carry clauses are not re-derived. Closes #3826. Refs #3323, #3794, #3819, #3398.
- **Design-critique comment-lead examples no longer copy a real model slug (#3824).** Fenced `model:` examples use a non-resolving placeholder instead of `grok-4.6`. The contract states that the lead is a self-attestation with no verifier, not provenance. Closes #3824. Refs #3628, #3815.
- **A stale PROJECT-DEFINITION lock is no longer cleared by guesswork (#3796).** Lock recovery used to delete whatever it found at the lock pathname. When an older deft version held that pathname with a plain file, deleting it released the only name that version recognises while its write was still in flight, so two processes could edit PROJECT-DEFINITION at once. A file left by an older version is now preserved and never moved; after one bounded attempt the timeout names the manual steps to clear it. Current-version locks are a directory published whole, so a late cleanup from a previous holder cannot remove a lock that replaced it, and recovery is automatic only when the recorded owner process is unambiguously gone -- a reused process id or an unreadable lock now stops for a human instead of being cleared on age. Every PROJECT-DEFINITION write also goes through one mutation capability bound to the file the lock actually took, closing two `wipCap` / `swarmSubagentBackend` writers that took no lock at all and several module-local copies of the loader and write path that could target a different file than the one held. A source inventory fails the build on any new bypass. Lock and loader diagnostics name a configured artifact by a fixed label rather than echoing its path.
- **Arm the shipped subagent-heartbeat path (#3730).** Dispatch creates `.deft-scratch/subagent-status/` at worktree create and pre-dispatch begin so `verify:subagent-alive --require-agent` can return REDISPATCH_OK instead of a missing-dir config error. Takeover after a killed worker is `swarm:pre-dispatch --action cancel` then begin. A stale gated ritual that blocks recovery names `session:start --rearm`. Envelopes tell workers to heartbeat and commit early. Related to #3613, not a child. Refs #1365, #2824, #3228. Closes #3730.
- **Greenfield setup exports and build handoff use one authority model (#3598).** `project:export-spec` includes proposed scopes for an internal export when scope selection is omitted, `prd:render` reads PROJECT-DEFINITION authority without creating a specification artifact, and generated banners name their actual xBRIEF source. Setup now routes through the cost decision before build, while full-spec compatibility remains supported.
- **Linked-worktree writes are gated against the worktree they land in.** Two isolated worktrees no longer contend over one lease, and a write into a separate repository is refused instead of borrowing the payload root's state. Refs #3794.
- **Design-critique ingest waits on the completed-arc record, not a catalog chip (#3806).** After `design-critique: synthesis accepted, because …` cites the accepted successor lean, `triage:accept` / `scope:promote` / `issue:ingest` proceed without `design-critique:triage-ready`, GitHub Triage, or same-session parent identity. Chip apply miss is non-blocking and is not `already exclusive`. A lone shape-matched comment does not unblock. Leftover `mechanism-shaped` / `judgmentGates` does not block. Closes #3806.

- **`verify:orphan-active` maps a missing `gh`/`ghx` to its own config exit.** When neither binary is on PATH, `ScmStubError` escaped `evaluate()` and became `directive: <raw>` via the dispatcher catch-all. The gate now returns code 2 with a `verify:orphan-active:` message. Exit 1 stays orphan-found. Unresolved GitHub lookup is unchanged. Closes #3774. Refs #3767, #3429, #2275.

- **`verify:orphan-active` no longer trusts a stale cached issue state (#3767).** A cache hit was returned unconditionally, so a twelve-hour-old cached `open` beat reality and suppressed the live read that would have corrected it. Issue state now resolves by query shape: scoped `--issue N` takes an authoritative read and stays fail-closed on unknown; the unscoped sweep resolves from one complete, fail-closed open-issue inventory (reusing #3752, measured 4.2 s constant against 14.2 s and 76.6 s for per-brief reads at the WIP cap) and stays fail-open on unknown so offline work is not network-authorized. A cache hit counts only within 15 minutes. Absence from the inventory is confirmed by one authoritative read before the gate reports shipped, and that result is reused when several briefs name the same issue. Every run prints the basis of its verdict — cache (with age), live, inventory, or unverified — so a pass is distinguishable from an unverified pass, and reads pin plain `gh` because `ghx` is itself a cache. Separate latency budgets are recorded for both modes. The offline crash (#3774) and `resolveBinary` binary preference (#3737) are separate. Closes #3767.
- **Setup persists branch policy through the namespaced writer (#3609).** Every Phase 2 track now writes an explicit branch-policy choice through the public policy CLI, verifies namespaced storage and xBRIEF conformance, and stops on dual bare/namespaced policy blocks. Policy writers reject ambiguous dual blocks without changing PROJECT-DEFINITION or the audit log and provide lossless recovery guidance.
- **Authorized writes are no longer refused by a hook that ran out of time (#3736).** The host mutation gate no longer makes a live forge call to re-check origin freshness -- that guarantee stays fail-closed at explicit `xbrief:preflight`, per brief -- and it now answers HEAD, worktree root, and branch from one `git` child instead of five. Under concurrent agents the hook was timing out or exiting non-zero, and the fail-closed deposit turned each of those into a false denial of legitimate work. The active-scope OR-fold, the nested 5s timeout, and `ghx` binary selection are unchanged. Closes #3736.
- **Greenfield setup exports and build handoff use one authority model (#3598).** `project:export-spec` includes proposed scopes for an internal export when scope selection is omitted, `prd:render` reads PROJECT-DEFINITION authority without creating a specification artifact, and generated banners name their actual xBRIEF source. Setup now routes through the cost decision before build, while full-spec compatibility remains supported.
- **Consumer toolchain checks honor the repository's npm or pnpm declaration (#3610).** `toolchain-check --consumer` and session preflight share strict package-manager precedence, probe only the selected manager, and give manager-specific remediation. npm-pinned projects no longer invoke a Corepack-rejected pnpm shim, and these toolchain probes no longer list go-task as required. Windows probes resolve an absolute PATH shim, preserve real Corepack failures, and run in the selected project root. Closes #3610. Refs #2197, #2761, #2765, #3335.
- **Refuse leftover swarm worktrees at the wrong commit (#3756).** Launch reuse of an already-registered worktree now compares commit identity, not presence, and hard-fails when the leftover HEAD does not match the requested base. The check is a snapshot at resolution time, not a pin on the worker's start revision. Does not re-point the leftover tree. Closes #3756.

- **A session that keeps working keeps its worktree lease (#3599).** Gated writes now renew `heartbeat_at`, so the 20-minute occupancy window runs from the owner's last write instead of from its claim; before this, a session that worked for hours still looked abandoned and was correctly stolen. The re-stamp is floored at a quarter of the window so the lease is not rewritten per event. `occupancy:steal` now reports the occupant's last write time, not only heartbeat age, so a mid-work occupant is visible before the steal. When the lease is inside the staleness window and that automatic renewal could not run, the write gate says so; a write that did renew the lease no longer reports it as going stale. New `occupancy:heartbeat` refreshes your own lease during long quiet stretches; it never claims a free worktree and never takes a foreign lease. Refreshing is bounded: a lease is dead 12 hours after `claimed_at` no matter how recently it beat, so a worktree left behind by a dead session is always reclaimable inside a day, and holding the occupant's session id no longer holds the tree forever. Twelve hours covers an overnight run whose agent finishes and then waits for you, since waiting produces no write to refresh on. Past the cap the tree reads as free to peers and the holder's own writes are refused until it re-claims — one command, and its work is untouched; allowing them would leave two live sessions writing one worktree. A renewal that finds the lease in another session's name now denies instead of writing under the record it started from. Closes #3599.

- **Host-spawned writes retain their occupancy owner (#3611).** Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor direct hooks use a versioned host session/conversation owner, and exact owner-requiring lifecycle commands receive the same explicit `--session-id`, keeping host, lease, and ritual identity aligned without inherited shell environment. No host-to-lease map or credential file is persisted. This is cooperative routing, not same-user authentication. Codex parent/subagents share a session owner; Claude uses the session; Cursor uses the conversation without an unverified subagent claim; Grok retains explicit/environment identity. Existing live UUID leases require a confirmed `session:start --steal` transition; bare steal remains lease-only and needs same-ID ritual alignment only when owners differ. Heartbeat renewal (#3599), hook reachability (#3742), and spawn occupancy (#3755) remain separate. Closes #3611.

- **Claim occupancy before creating swarm worktrees (#3649).** `swarm:launch` takes the occupancy lease before resolving or creating trees from `--worktree-map`. A foreign live occupant creates zero worktrees. If this launch newly claimed the lease and a later step fails, it releases that lease so close-out is not left with a stranded occupant. Does not change reuse of already-registered worktrees. Closes #3649.

- **Release Step 3 no longer issues one sequential `gh api` call per anchored issue (#3752).** Pre-flight vBRIEF lifecycle sync now loads the complete open-issue inventory in one paginated REST subprocess and treats anchors absent from that set as non-open, with fail-closed handling for truncated or malformed inventory. Step 3 reports anchor counts up front; `task release` usage documents `--allow-vbrief-drift`.

### Removed

## [0.107.0] - 2026-08-26
### Added
- Added — article-review Step 6.5 process-only critic pass before filing, with Step 5 mechanism inventory and Critic verdict section on filed issues. Refs #5694.
- Added — Prefer-A Recut-2 for `feedback:file`: complete open inventory dedup, closed retained-count window (500) with disposition tokens, open-match evidence comment (`commented-open-duplicate`), and `--on-closed=comment|create-anyway` without reopen. Refs #5099.
- Added — Helpers for reviewing a brief without creating a GitHub issue. These support file-based critic results, retained review records, and returning the accepted remedy to the same brief. Refs #5486.
### Changed

- **`adoption-blocker` is the canonical consumer hard-stop label.** It now covers any intended Directive flow (install, first session, update, `task check`, ship) with no reasonable workaround, not only first session. The label means classified as a blocker; its absence means not classified, never that a workaround exists. Classification requires body evidence (attempted alternatives, or why documented alternatives are not reasonable). An upgrade-path hard stop wears this label plus `Upgrade Blocker`; `Upgrade Blocker` alone does not rank. Closes #3650.

- **Stop 1 premises stay outside parent substantiation; Stop 1 records `refutation-target:` (#3672).** The contract now states why a pre-critic premise is excluded. Stop 1 write-backs record a non-binding `refutation-target:`. Not an audit marker; never blocks bind. Closes #3672.

- **Design-critique critics get a stated method (#3661).** The contract now says how to critique, at three distinct strengths, instead of only telling the parent how to dispatch. Stop 3's overloaded Charter heading is renamed to parent-facing dispatch rules. Closes #3661.

- **Leftover-completion PRs skip optional CI jobs (#3678).** When the diff against the merge base is only a completed xBRIEF and CHANGELOG, Windows, Go, merge-gate, smoke, and branch-gate do not run. The required TypeScript check still runs over a real lane. Closes #3678.

- **Design-critique panels share one input ceiling (#3660).** Same-round critics read comments only up to one id, fixed before any sibling posts. An N=3 panel gets three first-round posts and no default retry. The parent records the ceiling before dispatch. Closes #3660.

- **Design-critique walk is parent-disagreement only; empty all-accept map auto-stamps (#3640).** **walk** iterates disagree headings. **walk all** is the census (`walk findings one at a time` stays a one-release alias). A non-empty all-accept successor lean auto-posts the verified-claims table then `design-critique: synthesis accepted, because agents agreed (empty disagreement set)` and remaining-set-replaces to `triage-ready`. Stub critics and dispatch-fail do not stamp. Looks-good still does not bind. Thin skill pointer. Closes #3640.
- **Exclusive remaining-set replace for design-critique catalog chips (#3642).** Applying `design-critique:mechanism-shaped` or `design-critique:triage-ready` GET-drops the other catalog name and PUT/PATCHes that remaining set (`LabelClient.apply` / `mergeIssueLabels`). Parent write is `task scm:issue:design-critique-chip -- --issue N --chip triage-ready|mechanism-shaped` (not additive `scm:issue:edit --add-label`). No DELETE-then-POST window. Chip is list state, not consent. Closes #3642.

### Fixed

- **Posted successor lean before operator verbs after critic EXIT (#3741).** After a critic posts, the parent posts a successor lean with proposed per-heading takes before printing accept / retry differences / walk / walk all. That posted lean is the first operator surface. This supersedes #3627 for the first lean only. Operator confirm/amend binds takes. All-accept drafts still go through the offer. Auto-stamp and Bind path 1 require operator confirm and do not bind while same-round panel siblings remain unposted. Thin skill pointer. Content-contract tests lock the MUST, not live parent turns. Closes #3741. Refs #3434, #3627, ADR-005, ADR-006.
- **File writes no longer wait on triage-cache freshness (#3738).** A write still re-checks hook readiness. Cache drift stays a session and work-selection check, so activating a story no longer spends forge I/O on every Write. Closes #3738.
- **A verb mentioned in issue prose is no longer a stated acceptance command (#3721).** Inline backticks in a sentence stay advisory mentions. Labeled lines, `$` prompts, and fences still require promotion. An operator can list a capture under `literal_acceptance_not_commands` instead of promoting it. `scope:complete --help` now lists `--merge-commit` and `--pr`. Closes #3721.
- **Completed-write guard refuses oversized completed/ artifacts (#3679).** Newly added completed briefs larger than 1 MiB fail with the file path and the limit instead of an unbounded read. The lifecycle-stamp check is unchanged.
- **Concurrent launcher no longer tells you to set `readiness=sequential` (#3666).** Gate A now says a `parallel_safe: false` story is not eligible for `swarm:launch` and points at the interactive swarm-skill path, which is not gated by a non-zero `swarm:readiness` exit (exit 0 gates concurrent workers only). Gate B is unchanged. Closes #3666.
- **Scope provenance is no longer described as warn-only (#3712).** Agents now read that `--enforce` governs only the empty-scope case, and that a declared file scope without base approval fails closed. Test-boundary stays warn-only until authored policy; missing check-composition still fails closed. Closes #3712.

- **Build skill completes after merge, not before PR handoff (#3674).** The generated build skill told workers to run `scope:complete` before handoff, which a delivered story cannot satisfy. The pack now points at the existing post-merge lifecycle instead of restating it. Closes #3674.

- **GitHub worker validation names the expected user principal (#3665).** Deep auth checks take an expected login, compare it to `/user`, and derive the target repository. An installation-token `/user` 403 is reported as inapplicable, not unreachable; installation identity stays fail-closed until #3693. Closes #3665.

- **Design-critique panel row permits N≥3 on blast radius or an open solution space alone (#3657).** Drops the "No defensible presumption" conjunct. Charter and spend are recorded as two fields; `panel` is spend permission, not a third charter. Constrained-author trigger stays rejected. Supersedes #3434 disposition 5364365428 item 4.
- **Stop 4 retry critic posts stay in the auto-stamp denominator (#3640).** Comments after the id ceiling stay out of envelope except the critic's own Stop 4 retry post, including after the disagreement-map input ceiling. Do not chip `triage-ready` while those retry headings are undisposed.
- **Issue-eval open-PR census fails loud at the 5,000 page cap (#3648).** A full last page is an incomplete census, not a complete 5,000. Later PRs are not silently dropped from linkage verdicts.
- **Doctor no longer treats a bare `vbrief/` mention as a half-migrated layout pointer (#3637).** Left-bound `vbrief/` so `x-vbrief/` is not a hit. Child paths, `.vbrief.json`, and `vbrief:preflight` still rewrite; already-xbrief doctor copy points at hand-edit, not `migrate:xbrief`. Closes #3637. Refs #2154.
- **Win32 operator mint opens `\\.\CONIN$` with r+ (#3596 leftover).** Bare `CONIN$` ENOENT on a real console. Probe errors still refuse mint. Refs #3596, #3110.
- **Shell dest-form wrappers still see the verb after a post-flag env assignment (#3438 leftover).** `sudo -u root GIT_WORK_TREE=pkg git checkout -- file` stays recognized (fail-closed on work-tree). `sudo grep rm file` stays unclassifiable. Refs #3438.
- **Shell dest-form wrappers do not treat a later `rm` data token as the verb (#3438 leftover).** `sudo grep rm file` stays unclassifiable. Value-taking wrapper flags (`sudo -u`, `env -u`) still find the real verb. Refs #3438.
- **Shell dest-form treats escaped `$` / backtick as literal dest characters (#3438 leftover).** Double-quoted `\$` / `` \` `` and single-quoted `$` no longer fail closed as unresolved substitution under `shellDestForms: enforce`. Unescaped `"$TARGET"` and `` `cmd` `` still deny. Refs #3438, #3594.
- **Recognized Shell dest-forms hit the active-xBRIEF write gate, opt-in (#3438 / #3594).** **Off by default** (`plan.policy.runtimeAuthority.shellDestForms: "off" | "enforce"`), so this lands with no behaviour change for any consumer: Shell stays unrecognized and fail-open exactly as before. Set `"enforce"` to opt in, which turns on resolved-dest gating and fail-closed targets together. Unknown values and unreadable policy resolve to `off` and are reported by `validateRuntimeAuthority`. There is no `warn` state -- the hook emits no text on the allow path, so a warned denial would be indistinguishable from `git status`. When enforced: `git checkout -- <paths>`, `git restore`, and `rm`/`rmdir` in a single simple command go through `inspectMutationGates` with the Edit/Write exemptions (assist/scratch, proposed lifecycle, story `file_scope`). An absolute dest is checked soundly; a relative dest assumes the shell sits at the project root. Everything else recognized is denied without being resolved: compound commands, grouping and substitution, git context options (`-C`, `--work-tree`, `--git-dir`, `-c core.workTree`, `GIT_WORK_TREE=`), glob/variable dests, and a leading `~`. Cwd and git-context reconstruction was implemented and withdrawn -- the target depends on operator precedence, exit status, subshell boundaries, and git config, and each resolution rule produced its own bypass -- so the deny now teaches the rewrite (one simple command, absolute path). **This raises the floor; it does not close the Bash bypass class.** Fail-open and untracked: unrecognized mutators (`git reset --hard`, `git clean`, `git checkout` without `--`, `mv`, `sed -i`, `>` redirection), interpreters (`bash -c`, `python -c`), and non-literal verbs (`\rm`, `rm${IFS}x`) where even the fail-closed branch cannot see the verb. The gate is a guardrail for careless agents, not a boundary against adversarial ones -- threat model in `content/contracts/path-write-fence.md`. Cross-repo escape: an absolute out-of-root dest is allowed. The fail-closed branch reaches no exemptions, so an assist-posture compound scratch cleanup must be split per call. Refs #3438, #3594, #2711, #1802, #2625, #2885.

Read commands such as `git log make DESTDIR=` and `find -exec echo make DESTDIR=` stay unclassifiable. Already-denied `ruby` / `python3` / `dpkg-deb` / `xcopy` / `cp` stay denied. Closes #3545. - **UAT Shell residual after #3459: dest writers still plant authz, kill-switch, and approved-scope (#3529).** Under active UAT, remaining dest-form Shell writers classify as settings deny when they target `.deft/authz/**`, kill-switch basenames, or `.deft/approved-scope/**`. Unknown dest flags targeting those paths fail closed. Ordinary dests such as `/tmp` stay unclassifiable. Already-denied `cmd /c copy` / `ginstall` / `tsx` / `cp` stay denied. Closes #3529. ## [0.105.0] - 2026-08-19
### Security

- **UAT Shell residual after #3421: extra dest writers plant authz, kill-switch, and approved-scope (#3459).** Under active UAT, write-shaped Shell dests that #3421 missed classify as settings deny when they target `.deft/authz/**`, kill-switch basenames, or `.deft/approved-scope/**`. GNU coreutils `g*` prefixes and unknown dest flags targeting those paths fail closed. Ordinary dests such as `/tmp` stay unclassifiable. Already-denied `install` / `cp` / `git clone` / `Set-Content` stay denied. Closes #3459. Refs #3421, #3410, #3039.

### Added
- Added — article-review Step 6.5 process-only critic pass before filing, with Step 5 mechanism inventory and Critic verdict section on filed issues. Refs #5694.
- Added — Prefer-A Recut-2 for `feedback:file`: complete open inventory dedup, closed retained-count window (500) with disposition tokens, open-match evidence comment (`commented-open-duplicate`), and `--on-closed=comment|create-anyway` without reopen. Refs #5099.
- Added — Helpers for reviewing a brief without creating a GitHub issue. These support file-based critic results, retained review records, and returning the accepted remedy to the same brief. Refs #5486.
### Changed

- **Coverage floor is 75, measured under vitest 4 (#3512).** All four metrics drop 85 -> 75, identical on win32 and Linux CI. This is a recalibration, not a relaxation: vitest 4 replaced `v8-to-istanbul` with AST-aware `ast-v8-to-istanbul`, and the same suite reads **85.35% branches (46194/54121) under vitest 3** vs **81.23% (50892/62651) under vitest 4** — covered branches *rose* by 4,698 while the denominator grew by 8,530. The old number was never comparable to the new one. 75 is Google's published "commendable" band, an external anchor rather than a self-referential one; Inozemtseva & Holmes (ICSE 2014) found aggregate coverage only weakly predictive of defect detection once suite size is controlled. The floor is now a collapse detector, with per-change rigor belonging to the diff gate — a control that is **not yet at full strength** (`verify:forward-coverage` is new-file-existence only, #3514), so ~6pp of aggregate erosion is a knowingly accepted gap watched via `task coverage:hotspots`. The config stamps the instrument in-file, and the #2573 / #2630 contract tests now assert the *invariant* (one uniform floor, no platform carve) instead of a literal that rots on every recalibration. Refs #3512, #3514, #3480, #2573, #2630, #1310.
- **Vitest 4 restores Windows coverage file parallelism (#3480).** Upgrade `vitest` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` ^3→^4. Drop `fileParallelism: false`, the coverage-tightened `winActiveMaxWorkers` cap, `coverage.processingConcurrency: 1`, and the removed `poolOptions.maxForks` (now just `maxWorkers`). Occupancy-stress children spawn via `tsx` (vitest 4 dropped vite-node). Floor is owned by #3512 (75); this PR does not set it. Keep the win32 `coverage/.tmp` globalSetup until a full run proves #10117 is enough. Refs #2546, #2580, #2634, #3501, #3472, #3512.

- **`deft update --dry-run` dest plan is recorded port calls (ADR-004 / #3462).** Dest write, remove, chmod, and dest-mutating git/exec go through `containedWrite`/`containedRemove` plus `containedChmod`/`containedDestExec`. Dry-run binds that port in record mode. The three inventoried seams (GitHooksSeams, copyContent, runOrgForceOn) fold into it. Static ban covers dest-mutating `execFileSync("git", …)` on the update path (allowlist = port module). Planted `xbrief/vbrief.md` stays byte-identical. Printed exclusions label names OpenClaw `$HOME` skills until that site folds. Closes #3437. Refs #3462, ADR-004, PR 3453.
- **ADR-004: `deft update --dry-run` plan is a side-effect port; salvage independent 3453 pieces (#3462).** Records the accepted architecture (construction-level collection; PR 3453 replace; #3437 stays open). Routes `removeStaleMigratedFrameworkNarrative` through `containedRemove`, lands a static dest-mutation ban on that function, and plants obsolete `xbrief/vbrief.md` in the dry-run byte-identical fixture. Does not implement the port or close #3437 / PR 3453. Refs #3437, #3453, #3392, #3458.
- **Standing residual until resolved Greptile floor or same-fingerprint loop (#3448).** Review-cycle and swarm leftover classes A/B/C: already-touched-file leftovers stay in-AC (class A) until the resolved `#3095` floor (policy > dogfood 5 > consumer default 4) or the single **Same-fingerprint stop** (2 consecutive re-review observations, blocked handoffs count) in review-cycle Dual stop. Standing-order phrases (`until floor or loop` / `until greptile meets policy` / `pursue residuals until told otherwise`) apply to open cohort/plan units; one-shot `pursue residual` stays one pass. Halt-report resume line names leftover class, resolved floor, and standing vs one-shot. No new skill or verb. Refs #3273, #2881, #3095, #2442.
- **Replace leftover Python helpers with committed Node so CodeQL stops Analyze (python) here (#3427).** CI watchdog scripts are `.mjs`; `ci.yml` does not invoke `python3`. Consumer `deft-core-guard` still deposits a `python3` heredoc from a shared Go/TS embed (not a `.py` file). Pin check still matches `isUpgradePinPathContentAllowed`. Org CodeQL languages are unchanged. Closes #3427.
- **`deft update` stages only this-run installer-managed ledger paths, including tracked deletions (#3394).** Ledger minus allowlist is printed and left unstaged. Untracked deletes are filtered so they cannot fail the batch. Pre-existing consumer edits to Taskfile, package.json, or .gitignore are not staged. Closes #3394. Refs #3378, #3392, #3393.

### Fixed

- **`verify:ac` runs stated `plan.acceptance.commands` and stays in exit 0/1/2 (#3449).** The executor only injected that array for `derived`/`project_floor`, so a `rung=stated` brief with nine commands printed `passed` / `no stated commands` and never ran them. Empty literal ledger now falls through to `plan.acceptance.commands`. Printed pass is exit 0; other codes clamp to 1 or 2. `check` `cause:` skips go-task `engine:_ts-build` script echo and names the verb. Closes #3449. Refs #3284, #3267, #3334, #3497.
- **Land leftover completed-tracked artifact for #3506 (#3264 / #1358).** The #3506 xBRIEF stayed in `xbrief/active/` after squash of PR 3517. Moved to `xbrief/completed/`. Does not reopen or recut that issue. Refs #2321, #3476.
- **Fenced terminal transcript is not blocking acceptance (#3511).** Output-shaped fences (`[1/13]`, box drawing, `FAIL`/`Error:`) are not captured as stated commands. A prose/fence/inline safety rejection is advisory even when the plan has no structured `verify_commands`. A genuinely unsafe command in a structured field still blocks. The #3502 and #3506 phantom ledgers complete without `--force` or rewriting the issue. A transcript skip that leaves zero captured commands on a project with a suite floor does not silently empty-pass. `FAIL`/`FAILED`/`Error:` skip does not treat `--fail-fast` / `--failOnError` / `--no-fail` or flag values (`--filter fail`, `--grep FAIL`) as transcript output. Ledger `waived`/`not_applicable` disposition remains leftover. Closes #3511. Refs #3484, #3497, #3502, #3267, #3334.
- **Land leftover completed-tracked artifact for #3511 (#3264 / #1358).** The #3511 xBRIEF stayed in `xbrief/active/` after squash of PR 3518. Moved to `xbrief/completed/` via `scope:complete`. Does not reopen or recut that issue. Refs #2321, #3476.
- **Archive member names keep original git path bytes (#3490 residual).** `archiveRel` stays a display string, but zip/tar member names are the original `-z` bytes (POSIX `/`). Archiver's string `name` is UTF-8; invalid bytes go through a marked latin1 name and the nested `setName` / PAX path Buffer copy. ZIP leaves the UTF-8 language-encoding flag off for those raw names. Fail-closed git enumerate and surprise untracked are unchanged. Refs #3490.
- **Invalid-byte git paths stay in the archive set (#3490 residual).** `realpathSync` / `lstatSync` take Buffer paths so latin1 `-z` names are not re-encoded as UTF-8 and skipped. Canonical root bytes come from `realpath` `encoding: "buffer"`, not `Buffer.from(resolve(root), "utf8")`. Fail-closed git enumerate and surprise untracked are unchanged. Refs #3490.
- **`git ls-files -z` archive listing splits on NUL bytes, not a UTF-8 stream (#3490 residual).** Spawn captures a Buffer, splits on `0x00`, and decodes each path. Non-UTF-8 git path bytes stay intact. Fail-closed when git cannot enumerate tracked files. Refs #3490.
- **Release archive is tracked files plus an explicit generated-output allowlist (#3490).** `buildArchive` no longer packs every untracked file that misses a basename denylist. Untracked host trees cannot change the artifact. A surprise untracked path in the resolved set fails closed. A symlink *to* the checkout as `--root` is inside; a symlink *out of* the tree still fails closed. Closes #3490. Refs #3487, #2953.
- **Consumer AGENTS.md names `session:ready` on the #1149 ritual line (#3506).** The deposit pointer now includes the one-shot recovery verb (`session:start` + gated ritual + cache recovery). `agents_entry_contract` markers follow. Closes #3506. Refs #3500, #2993, #1149, #1309, PR 3509.
- **CI merge-gate exempts `verify:branch` on a post-merge master checkout (#3499).** The documented `DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT=1` env is set on the two `task check:merge` steps only. Local `task check` and git hooks stay fail-closed. Closes #3499. Refs #1704, #747.
- **Land leftover completed-tracked artifact for #3502 (#3264 / #1358).** The #3502 xBRIEF stayed in `xbrief/active/` after squash, so `verify:orphan-active` failed on later PRs. Moved to `xbrief/completed/`. Does not reopen or recut that issue. Refs #2321.
- **Gated ritual CLI failure prints `session:ready` recovery (#3506).** Direct `verify:session-ritual --tier=gated` now appends the one-shot recovery line and the audited `session:start -- --defer cache_fresh=<reason>` soft path. `--json` includes `recovery_tier`. Tracking: #3506. Refs #3500, #2993, #1149, #3507.
- **Agent-host working state is gitignored (#3502).** `.claude/worktrees/` and `.claude/settings.local.json` join the canonical baseline in both shipped surfaces (`CANONICAL_GITIGNORE_BASELINE` and the `deft-install` Go twin) and this repo's own `.gitignore`. Un-ignored agent worktrees leave a permanently dirty tree, which refuses release Step 1 — it cost three of five v0.105.0 cut attempts, and every consumer that dispatches subagents hits the same wall. Selective by design: `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/skills/` and `.claude/commands/` are managed deposits and stay trackable, per the #1144 hybrid rule that forbids blanket directory ignores. #3487 fixed what Directive's walks enumerate; this fixes what git sees. Closes #3502. Refs #3487, #1144, #1942.

- **`scope:complete` no longer refuses acceptance that verify:ac passes (#3497).** A derived-rung brief with non-empty executable `plan.acceptance.commands` whose command exited 0 was refused with "scope:complete refuses empty or failing acceptance", printed directly under four lines saying the run was green. Two readers, one artifact, two stories. `verify:ac` and `scope:complete` now share one resolver (`packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/acceptance-resolver.ts`): one option profile per reader and one verdict, so the refusal names the predicate that fired and the value it read (`clause-walk-failed — clause walk read 0 verified, 4 unverifiable, 0 failed`) instead of asserting one that did not. The wrong predicate was the #3323 clause walk: a clause the static walk *cannot decide* was treated as a failure, so an all-unverifiable prose clause set refused a brief whose stated command had just exited 0. Unverifiable clauses now block only when nothing else verified the product; a clause the shipped artifact contradicts still blocks unconditionally, and genuinely empty and genuinely failing acceptance are still refused (#3357 is unchanged and correct). `verify:ac` also stops rendering "verify:ac passed" for a result it refused. The remediation stops recommending an inert remedy: `task verify:ac` verifies and never writes the brief — it is the verifier, and a verifier that authors the acceptance it then checks is not a gate — so the message names the stamping surfaces instead. Closes #3497. Refs #3357, #3323, #3284, #3267, #3334.
- **`verify:ac` honours the #3484 advisory demotion that `verify:literal-ac` already did (#3497).** A prose-derived safety rejection on a plan that states structured acceptance commands is demoted to advisory and printed as "do NOT block" — then `verify:ac` blocked on it anyway, returning `rejected-noop`, because it sniffed the refusal reason back out of its own rendered advisory block. It now reads the structured blocking ledgers and skips the advisory tail. A no-op command stated *structurally* still blocks. The demoted ledger also survives the derived/floor direct-run path instead of vanishing. Closes #3497. Refs #3484, #3486, #3396.
- **`routing-set` CLI takes an injected environment; the openclaw test constructs its own (#3494).** `routingSetMain(argv, environ = process.env)` now carries the same env seam `resolveDispatchProvider` and `resolveRoutingPath` already had, and threads it to both. `routing-set-openclaw.test.ts` passes `{ OPENCLAW: "1" }` instead of subtracting a denylist of known hosts from the ambient `process.env`. That denylist rotted twice — #3492 added the Claude Code vars but missed `DEFT_HAS_CLAUDE_AGENT` and `DEFT_AGENT_RUNTIME`, both of which outrank OpenClaw — so any host setting them could not run `task check`. The test now states exactly what it asserts and no future host signal can silently invalidate it. Production behaviour is unchanged: with no injected env the CLI still reads `process.env`. Closes #3494. Refs #3492, #3134, #2875.
- **`routing-set-openclaw` test is no longer defeated by ambient host env (#3492).** The test cleared a denylist of hosts before asserting OpenClaw wins, but never learned about Claude Code, which #3134 added at *higher* precedence in `resolveDispatchProvider`. An ambient `CLAUDECODE` therefore failed the assertion — meaning `task check` could not pass when run from inside Claude Code, a supported and dogfooded agent host, and it blocked the v0.105.0 release cut at Step 5. Clears `CLAUDECODE` / `CLAUDE_CODE` / `DEFT_PROBE_CLAUDE_CODE` alongside the existing Cursor / Grok / CI vars. Product routing behaviour is unchanged and correct. Making host-resolution tests hermetic by construction (inject the environment rather than partially clearing `process.env`) is tracked as follow-up on #3492. Closes #3492. Refs #3134, #2875.

- **One shared "not product source" exclusion set behind all four walks (#3487).** `verify-stubs` `EXCLUDE_DIRS`, `validate-links` `EXCLUDE_DIRS`, `default-extractor` `SKIP_DIRS`, and `build-dist` `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES` were four independently hand-maintained literals that had drifted from each other, and none knew about agent-host working directories: three Claude Code worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` added ~11,000 walkable entries to this repo (9,128 → 20,393) that no set skipped, and `build-dist` would have packed every one of them into a release archive built on that host. All four now extend `NON_PRODUCT_DIRS` in `packages/core/src/fs/non-product-dirs.ts` — VCS metadata, dependency trees, build output, tool caches, `.deft-scratch` / `swarm-worktrees`, and `.claude`. Each walk keeps its own extras (`tests` / `vendor` / `history` / `scripts`; `.planning` / `specs`; `build`; `htmlcov` / `coverage` / `.coverage`) and `build-dist` keeps its `extraExcludes` options bag. Every set is a strict superset of what it excluded before, so nothing newly enters a walk; the only archive-content change is `.claude`, which holds no tracked path in this repo. `.openclaw` is deliberately absent — there is no project-level `.openclaw/`, the host state dir is `~/.openclaw`, and inventing a project one is forbidden by `content/docs/openclaw-agent-host.md`; `.cursor` / `.grok` / `.codex` / `.github` hold committed Directive deposits, not working state. `non-product-dirs.test.ts` fails on divergence instead of leaving it to be found by measurement a year later. Closes #3487. Refs #3481, #2953, #2954, #1656.
- **`sortedRglob` prunes excluded directories during the walk (#3481).** `verify:stubs` descended into every directory and consulted `EXCLUDE_DIRS` only afterwards, per-file, so a populated `.deft-scratch/` was enumerated in full and then discarded — 5,244,941 entries and a 406s walk on a 218-worktree host, 749s end-to-end for a gate that reads only `.py` / `.go` / `.sh`. `walk` now skips a directory whose basename is in `EXCLUDE_DIRS` before recursing; the per-file check stays for callers passing explicit paths. Completes the stated intent of #2953, whose diff added `.deft-scratch` / `swarm-worktrees` to the set but never touched the walk. The new test asserts on `sortedRglob`'s output rather than on the filter — the assertion whose absence let #2953 ship without effect. Closes #3481. Refs #2953, #2954, #3479, #1656.
- **Cohort-close MUST named `task xbrief:validate`, which did not exist (#3483).** The #2109 rename added `xbrief:`-prefixed verbs only where the surface was rewritten, so four MUST/⊗-level swarm instructions named a verb that exited 200. `xbrief:validate` and `xbrief:activate` now ship as aliases of their `vbrief:` originals (mirroring `xbrief:preflight`); the legacy spellings stay live and `task check` gate ids are unchanged. The `xbrief` Taskfile include is no longer `optional`. Two hedges that papered over the gap are gone (`commands.md` "(or `task xbrief:validate`)", sync skill "if available"). A new content contract resolves every `task <verb>` named at MUST/⊗ level in the swarm skill against the real task graph; it also caught `task verify:gh-auth` (#1557), which never had a task wrapper over the `github-auth-modes` engine verb and now does. Closes #3483. Refs #1487, #2109, #3479.
- **Mid-line `verify:` in prose no longer captures a phantom acceptance command (#3484).** The literal-AC scraper matched a label token anywhere in a line and took the rest of the line as the command body, so an ordinary sentence like `That verb is filesystem-only. verify:orphan-active goes green.` became a "command" that swallowed the remaining paragraph, failed the safety allowlist, and permanently blocked `scope:complete` with no disposition path. A labeled command must now start its own line (after an optional bullet or number marker); mid-sentence commands must live in a fence, a `$`/`>` prompt, or an inline backtick span — forms that have a real terminator. Structured also beats scraped: when `swarm.verify_commands` or `plan.acceptance.commands` is stated and non-empty, prose-derived safety rejections are demoted to advisory (reported in the gate message and as `advisory_rejected` in `verify:literal-ac -- --capture-only`) instead of blocking; rejections whose provenance is a structured field still block. The safety allowlist and shell-metacharacter rejection are unchanged. Closes #3484. Refs #3267, #3476.
- **`verify:completed-tracked` fail-open paths closed (#3476 review).** Three fallbacks let a DONE gate whose purpose is fail-closed pass an unlanded issue. (1) `resolveDeliveryTip` no longer falls back to `HEAD` when neither `origin/<deliveryBranch>` nor `<deliveryBranch>` resolves — on a shallow clone, unfetched worktree, or `fetch-depth:1` checkout that checked the very feature branch whose land was in question; an unresolvable tip is now an error naming `--tip`. (2) `--issue N` matching is repo-scoped: a foreign repo's same-numbered issue no longer survives the filter, suppresses synthesis of the requested issue, and green-skips it with its own open state. (3) Under `--skip-gh`, an explicitly named `--issue` with no cached state now fails closed instead of exiting 0; the unscoped corpus scan keeps its offline allowance for uncached issues. Refs #3476, #3264, #1358.
- **Unrecognized host is disclosure, not a launch gate (#3469).** `verify:routing` (advise and enforce / launch) prints a dedicated honesty line when the provider is `unknown`: host unrecognized, which env/probes were empty, that dispatch is still allowed, and which `unknown` pin or inherit will be used. Exit is 0. `unknown` pins stay valid and are named. `resolveDispatchProvider` honors the same Grok probes `probeMonitoringTier` already uses (`DEFT_HAS_SPAWN_SUBAGENT`, `DEFT_PROBE_GROK_BUILD`, `DEFT_PROBE_SPAWN_SUBAGENT`). Live routing key is `grok`; a `grok-build` file key is read as grok or ignored without blocking. `GROK_BUILD` alone is not cloud-headless. Closes #3469.
- **`feedback:file` repeated `--context` flags accumulate (#3454).** Collected values join with newlines so `context` stays a string. Closes #3454.
- **`deft update --dry-run` leads with deposit vs content version skew (#3437).** When the recorded install manifest and the content package disagree, that line is first (`manifest X -> content Y`). `--json` adds `previous_version`, `content_version`, and `deposit_refresh_pending`. No file-level plan (`strategy` / `planned_paths` / `planned_file_count`) — that waits on #3462. Refs #3437. Prior art: halted PR 3453.
- **Init-deposit dest deletes go through the write chokepoint (#3456).** Named dest deletes and temp cleanups use `containedRemove`. Schema projection validates planned content, not stale dest a skipped write would replace. Plan-mode / `deft update --dry-run` leaves the tree unchanged (keystone hash). Closes #3456. Refs #3392, #3437.
- **Occupancy lock races (#3433).** Release re-reads under the occupancy lock so close-out cannot delete a replacement claim. Lock wait unlinks only a lock this waiter acquired, or a lock whose owner PID is proven dead — not a live writer.
- **After-merge orphan-active is a per-issue check (#3429).** `task verify:orphan-active -- --issue N` runs the same gate for one origin. Confirmed shipped (closed issue or merged PR) exits 1 and prints `task scope:complete -- <path>`. Unresolved GitHub lookup still exits 1 but prints a retry remediation, not scope:complete. `drive-to: merge-ready` DONE requires that check exit 0 after merge. Consumer agents-entry distinguishes shipped vs unresolved. `agentsMdBudget.managedMaxLines` 160→162 and `absoluteMaxBytes` 15200→15400 for that pointer. Closes #3429. Refs #2321, #1487, #1358.
- **Run-summary stream uses one workspace `session_id` and a uniform envelope (#3399).** Emitters resolve identity as explicit option → `DEFT_SESSION_ID` → ritual-state → last JSONL `session_id` → mint only when no workspace session exists. Component names (`verify-ac`, `clause-derivation`) live in optional `component`, not `session_id`. `ac_pass_bank` goes through `RunSummaryEmitter` (`event: "ac_pass_bank"`); the disk ledger stays camelCase. The session:start fallback denominator of `1` is withdrawn. Share is unevaluable without a host/harness value (`DEFT_TOTAL_TOOL_TURNS` / `DEFT_MAX_TURNS` / `hostMaxTurns`); known values carry `denominator_source` (`harness_actual` | `host_planned`). Refs #3352, #3356, #3285, #3350.
- **slices.jsonl umbrellas refresh current-shape and close on `all-children-merged` (#3428).** `task vbrief:reconcile:umbrellas` walks `xbrief/.triage-cache/slices.jsonl` as well as epic xBRIEFs. Forge child state updates the §1152 comment. When the signal is `all-children-merged` and every child is closed, the still-open umbrella gets one REST close plus a comment naming the signal and child numbers. `wave-1-merged` and `manual` stay open. Re-run is a no-op. Closes #3428. Refs #3377, #3378.
- **No-op acceptance commands fail closed at capture and stamp (#3396).** `true`, `:`, `false`, bare `exit`, and assertion-free `echo`/`printf`/`test` with constant args are refused. One remediation: acceptance commands must be able to fail. `source_rung` is `stated` only with a recorded statement span; a restamp cannot raise the rung without that provenance. Events record `rejected-noop`. Closes #3396. Refs #3267, #3284, #3334, #3387.

- **UAT Shell residual after #3400/#3410: dest-form plant of authz, kill-switch, and approved-scope (#3421).** Under active UAT, residual dest forms (`git clone` / `worktree` / `submodule`, `ex`, `dos2unix -n`, `aws s3 sync` / `s3api get-object`, `pijul`, `pg_dump -f` / `--file`, `convert` / `magick`, `fossil --workdir=`, `New-Item`) that write into `.deft/authz/**`, plant `.deft-directive-disable` / `.no-deft-directive`, or write `.deft/approved-scope/**` classify as settings deny (not unclassifiable allow). Unknown write-shaped dest flags (`--workdir` / `--file` / `-f` / `-Path`) targeting those paths also fail closed. Ordinary dests such as `/tmp` stay unclassifiable. A protected source operand on last-positional dest bins (`aws` / `convert` / `magick`) that writes elsewhere is not a dest plant. Unlisted git globals consume the next token so a later dest writer is still seen; boolean globals (`--no-pager`) do not. A later kill-switch write after an `aws`/`convert`/`magick` segment still settings-deny. `env` / assignment prefixes do not hide last-positional dest ownership. Wrapper option values (`env -C`) and timeout durations are not the dest-owning bin. Unlisted git option values are skipped unless they are a git subcommand. `.deft/authz` and `.deft/approved-scope` match only as path segments. In-place `mogrify` still treats a protected operand as dest. `--file` on read-shaped bins is not a dest plant. Already-denied `cmake` / `curl -o` / `ed` / `nvim` / `fossil --workdir PATH` / `aws s3 cp` stay denied. Closes #3421. Refs #3382, #3410, #3039.
- **Mint writes approved-scope record + preimage as a fail-closed pair (#3385).** Dest publish is two-phase under a per-plan lock: both dests land as `.next`, then dests copy from that pair. Recover finishes the flip or restores the bak pair (or neither dest) without a remint. Dead-owner lock files are reclaimed. A caught dest failure still restores or clears dests as a pair. Residual of PR #3414.
- **Obsolete xbrief schema delete is ledgered so update can stage it (#3418).** `syncConsumerXbriefSchemas` removes dest-only `vbrief-core.schema.json` through `containedRemove`. Ledger intersection can `git add` the tracked deletion. Closes #3418. Refs #3394, #3392.

- **Official Cursor adapter deletes no longer trip mixed-core-and-app (#3393).** A framework-only update that removes the retired hook adapter is installer-managed, not app. Other consumer hooks stay app-owned. Consumers on `pull_request_target` or pinned workflow refs see the old guard for one PR. Closes #3393. Refs #3378.
- **Derived clauses must trace to the task statement (#3398).** A stamp of only implementation symbol-grep clauses fails closed: derive clauses from the statement's testable constraints. Derivation now records an ambiguity attestation (none_found or an ambiguous clause with readings), and acceptance_stamp telemetry includes provenance_counts and ambiguity_attested. `triage:accept`, `scope:activate` / `scope:promote`, `vbrief:reconcile:graph`, `swarm:complete-cohort`, and `swarm:finalize-cohort` print the refused-stamp remediation. Closes #3398. Refs #3360, #3323.

- **`scope:record-approved-scope` uses the #3110 human-presence mint gate (#3384).** Shared TTY / controlling-terminal / `--confirm` / typed `mint` / agent-CI refuse; `--actor` is display-only. New records omit `xbriefBodyDigest`. Wave 1 records have no `intentDigest` and are legacy under #3385. Closes #3384. Refs #3376, #3110.
- **scope:complete: ancestry on deliveryBranch is delivery; PR base is provenance (#3380).** A merge commit that is an ancestor of refreshed `origin/<deliveryBranch>` completes as delivered even when `prBase` is develop. Ancestry miss stays `merged_to_integration`. Remediations name `--merge-commit` and typed `deliveryBranch`. Documents squash-sync ancestry break. Closes #3380.

- **Failing verify:ac walks emit a walk-level verification fingerprint (#3397).** A fail then a later pass with a different command set on the same check id flags; an honest same-command product fix does not. Shrinking command-set delta is included on the flag. The #3322 detector stays. Closes #3397. Refs #3322, #3396.
- **engine:_ts-build: trailing no-op for go-task <3.52 (#3381).** Older go-task treats an untaken last if/fi as exit 1, so consumer deposits fail every non-runtime `task deft:*`. A colon after the outer fi keeps the skip-build path exit 0. Closes #3381.
- **One SoT for advisory doctor fails; dirty copy no longer says address findings (#3379).** `deriveExitCode` and `cmdDoctor` share `DOCTOR_ADVISORY_FAIL_CHECKS`. A fail is a warning when `data.advisory` is true or the name is in that set. Dirty status / throttle hint names `--full` as re-probe only and says hard errors block writes, advisory warnings do not. Closes #3379. Refs #3372.
- **`slice:record-existing` / `slice:list` print the live triage-cache slices log, not the leftover `.eval` path (#3386).** Closes #3386.
- **UAT Shell residual after #3354: dest-form writers plant authz or kill-switch (#3382).** Under active UAT, residual dest forms (`cmake -E copy`, `script`, `gallery-dl -d`, `megadl --path`, `ncftpget`, `git apply --directory`, VCS checkout writers, editors) that write into `.deft/authz/**` or plant `.deft-directive-disable` / `.no-deft-directive` classify as settings deny (not unclassifiable allow). Unknown write-shaped dest flags (`-d` / `--path` / `--directory`) targeting those paths also fail closed. Ordinary dests such as `/tmp` stay unclassifiable. Already-denied `curl -o` / `nc -o` stay denied. Closes #3382. Refs #3354, #3039.
- **scope:complete acceptance walk is bank-aware (#3387).** A matching #3285 green bank with the same product-state hash is the walk result; mismatch, missing, or stale hash still runs the full walk. Same-session verify:ac can serve from_cache. Acceptance events record `served_from` bank, cache, or executed. Empty or failing acceptance still refuses (#3357). Product-state globs include wildcard-selected, character-class, mixed ordinary/hidden, recursive `**` nested dotfiles, files under hidden directories, negated `[!a]` classes, recursive brace alternatives, and extglob `@(a|b)` scopes; directory walks terminate on symlink cycles; porcelain `-z` and the non-NUL fallback keep invalid UTF-8 path bytes without U+FFFD and hash those files through byte FS paths; directory and glob walks keep invalid-byte names; failed git status is incomplete, not a clean tree; dirty submodule directories hash their contents; unwalkable gitlinks fingerprint the recorded SHA; fallback porcelain does not treat ` -> ` inside an ordinary path as a rename; wildcard prefixes before `**` still walk hidden directories; C-quoted rename destinations and UTF-8 octal escapes still decode.

## [0.104.0] - 2026-08-14

> Always-on writing bar (clarity, simplicity, brevity), telemetry dead-surface detector, ceremony-dial evidence, and done-gate/session/UAT/origin-freshness fixes.

> Always-on writing bar: clarity, simplicity, brevity for documents and communications (#3368).

### Added
- Added — article-review Step 6.5 process-only critic pass before filing, with Step 5 mechanism inventory and Critic verdict section on filed issues. Refs #5694.
- Added — Prefer-A Recut-2 for `feedback:file`: complete open inventory dedup, closed retained-count window (500) with disposition tokens, open-match evidence comment (`commented-open-duplicate`), and `--on-closed=comment|create-anyway` without reopen. Refs #5099.
- Added — Helpers for reviewing a brief without creating a GitHub issue. These support file-based critic results, retained review records, and returning the accepted remedy to the same brief. Refs #5486.
### Changed

### Fixed

- **`verify:ac` no longer fail-closes on historical completed xBRIEFs that lack `plan.metadata` (#3375).** Parseable pre-#3357 completed files are not this-session unreadable targets, so `task check` after `session:start` can soft-skip when nothing completed this session. Broken JSON and a same-session marker at an unreadable path still fail closed. Closes #3375. Refs #3357.

- **Advisory `completed-open-items` no longer fail-closes doctor or Write/Task (#3372).** `cmdDoctor` mapped unlisted check fails to `severity: error`, so `lastErrorCount > 0` and gated ritual / PreToolUse blocked the official recovery (edit completed JSON). The check is now a warning through the findings mapper, same allowlist pattern as other exit-exempt checks. Finding still names artifact paths. `completed-lifecycle-consistency` and new `scope:complete` stay fail-closed. Closes #3372. Refs #3242, #2862.

- **session:start emits `tool_turn_denominator` so ritual share is computable (#3356).** `emitKnownToolTurnDenominator` stayed silent unless `DEFT_TOTAL_TOOL_TURNS` was set, so field streams never got a denominator. session:start now always emits one when `DEFT_RUN_SUMMARY_PATH` is set: harness actuals, else `DEFT_MAX_TURNS` / host `maxTurns`, else this CLI invocation (1). Share is `ritual_events / denominator`. Seq lock protocol unchanged. Closes #3356. Refs #3352, #3320, #3282.
- **Acceptance telemetry fires on promote/activate/verify, not only issue:ingest (#3355).** `acceptance_stamp` emits when `plan.acceptance` is first written or materially changed on those verbs. `verify:ac` emits an `acceptance` outcome on every terminal path (config-error, soft-missing, soft-empty, run-pass, run-fail). Closes #3355. Refs #3323, #3334, #3360, #3282.
- **Origin freshness is fail-closed at `xbrief:preflight` (#3363).** When an origin-linked brief's live GitHub `updated_at` is newer than `xBRIEFInfo.updated`, preflight exits 1 and names re-read body+comments then dispose -- it does not auto-write origin onto the brief. All GitHub issue URLs in Origin/description are freshness-checked, not only the first. Refinement/sync prose now matches `reconcile:issues` (no stale-content bucket). Closes #3363.
- **scope:complete then check no longer vacates the done-gate (#3357).** `scope:complete` runs the verify:ac walk as a hard precondition on the completing brief and fails closed on empty or failing acceptance (item disposition is not a substitute). Check composition still uses `--soft-missing-xbrief` when no story was active this session, but a same-session complete targets the just-completed brief under `xbrief/completed` instead of skipping. One remediation string when that target cannot be read. Closes #3357. Refs #3334, #3267, #3284.
- **Hand-authored briefs run #3323 clause derivation on activate/promote (#3360).** When `plan.acceptance` is absent, empty-with-none_stated, or command-only-without-clauses, `scope:activate` / `scope:promote` decompose Overview/task-statement narratives, stamp `clauses[]` with `ambiguous`/`readings`/`chosen_reading`, and emit `acceptance_stamp`. The #3334 remedy names that derive step. Headless: records a chosen reading, never a blocking question. Closes #3360. Refs #3323, #3334, #3355, #3351.
- **UAT Shell residual after #3336: further write bins plus slices.jsonl leaf diversion (#3354).** Under active UAT, residual bins (`nc`/`netcat`/`7zz`/`msgfmt`/`msgcat`/`lz4`/`lzop`/`unrar`/`rar`/`aunpack`/`atool`/`ftpget`/`tftp`/`sqlite3`/`crane`/`objcopy`) that write into `.deft/authz/**` or plant `.deft-directive-disable` / `.no-deft-directive` classify as settings deny (not unclassifiable allow). Dest flags cover `-o`/`--output`/`--outfile` and 7zz attached `-oDIR`; unknown write-shaped dest flags targeting those paths also fail closed. `slices.jsonl` append routes through `containedWrite` so a leaf symlink cannot divert the write. Ordinary non-authz dests such as `/tmp` stay unclassifiable. Already-denied `ncat`/`7z`/`msguniq` peers stay denied. Closes #3354. Refs #3336, #3288, #3039.
- **Run-summary seq lock reclaims only dead or unknown owners (#3361).** `.seq.lock` stores a pid+nonce token. A waiter does not delete a live holder's lock by mtime. Release unlinks only when the token still matches this holder. Fail-open after the bounded wait is unchanged (#3282). Residual of #3350. Closes #3361. Refs #3353, #3350, #3282.
- **Run-summary file-destination seq continues across CLI processes (#3350).** A new emitter that appends to an existing `DEFT_RUN_SUMMARY_PATH` JSONL seeds `seq` from the current line count, so N events across processes are `1..N`. Concurrent writers serialize count-then-append with a sibling lock; abandoned locks are reclaimed when the owner process is dead or the token is unreadable (#3361). Stdout destination stays per-process. Closes #3350. Refs #3320, #3282.

- Added — article-review Step 6.5 process-only critic pass before filing, with Step 5 mechanism inventory and Critic verdict section on filed issues. Refs #5694.
- Added — Prefer-A Recut-2 for `feedback:file`: complete open inventory dedup, closed retained-count window (500) with disposition tokens, open-match evidence comment (`commented-open-duplicate`), and `--on-closed=comment|create-anyway` without reopen. Refs #5099.

### Fixed

- **verify:ac product-oracle check ids are namespaced per active scope (#3337).** Multi-active sessions no longer share one global `verify:ac` check id, so a fail from story A and a pass from story B cannot false-deny as an unresolved method-change sequence. Same-scope fail then different-method pass still fails closed without independent re-derivation. Residual of #3322 / PR #3333. Closes #3337. Refs #3322, #3333.

Python body lines are now indented with the run block; the installer-managed allowlist is one ERE per line via `grep -vE -f` (no ~5k-char shell line). Mix detection semantics unchanged. Consumers need `deft update` / re-deposit to receive the fixed workflow. Closes #3345. Refs #1430, #3193, #3127.
